subject: health
title: Mastery check: confidentiality basics
essentialQuestion: How can understanding health literacy, systems, and support help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Confidentiality means information is handled with privacy, but rules and safety exceptions vary by setting, age, and location; ask a provider what is private before sharing details.
Match the need to the appropriate service or administrative step, ask about access, cost, and privacy, and confirm what action or document comes next.
For confidentiality basics, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Create a health-information verification protocol and support map using fictional examples.
studentTask: Route two supplied fictional needs involving confidentiality basics. For each, choose the appropriate service or administrative step, list two access or privacy questions to ask, and write the next action the fictional person can complete without disclosing unrelated details.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in confidentiality basics; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the confidentiality basics task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. extensionChallenge: Apply confidentiality basics under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
